titulo: Pencil Animation: To Us, Parties Are Spiritual Events
caption:
Pencil Animation: To Us, Parties Are Spiritual Events

A pencil draws a listener at a party. Everything they start making out of the music gets erased, and the crowd around them is redrawn dancing. Her question, retold: how would her life change if she danced more, listened more.

Our words, our view: "Parties are godlike events, spiritual events, where people share their energy through music and through their bodies in one of the most primal ways." Try it: go dancing with people, phone in your pocket. When did you last dance with people?

From "everyone wants to be a DJ, no one wants to dance" by Dani Offline, offline soul, 11 Sep 2025: https://danioffline.substack.com/p/everyone-wants-to-be-a-dj-no-one . The sentence about parties, the "try it" and the question are ours: our words, our view. Dani Offline did not make or endorse this video. Her essay and every NAOS strategy are on the NAOS page linked in our bio.

More strategies: link in bio.

The eraser leaves a ghost of every rubbed line. Her question, retold: how would her life change if she danced more, listened more.
Our words, our view: "Parties are godlike events, spiritual events, where people share their energy through music and through their bodies in one of the most primal ways." Try it: go dancing with people, phone in your pocket.

alt: Pencil animation on warm paper. A crowd is seen from above in loose graphite, with one figure in the middle wearing headphones round the neck. The title "everyone wants to be a DJ, no one wants to dance" and "dani offline" are lettered by hand. In red pencil, a notebook, a phone held up and a quick run of small icons are drawn over the figure. Each one is rubbed out and leaves a pink eraser ghost. The crowd fades, then is redrawn darker with arms up, dancing. The figure dances with them until its outline joins the crowd's lines. Our sentence about parties is lettered whole with "our words, our view" under it and spoken aloud. A phone-shaped bump shows in the figure's pocket. End card on the paper: when did you last dance with people? and the credit.
